mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 2.5% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity prices, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or the 5-day discount rate change is not significantly negative (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months indicate deflationary pressure, which lowers real discount rates and tends to boost equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05), or the 3-month CPI decline is not sustained beyond the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month coincides with rising consumer confidence and reduced recession risk, which amplifies risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average (IC > 0.10) or unemployment falls below 3.5% during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month signals weakening aggregate demand, which compresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's (IC > -0.10) or INDPRO recovers by >2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in manufacturing activity (HOUST) above 1,000 indicates supply-side expansion that reduces cost pressures and supports higher corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC < 0.05) or HOUST growth is not sustained for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment claims (UNRATE) above 230,000 suggest deteriorating labor market conditions, which can depress consumer spending and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 230,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day average (IC > -0.10) or UNRATE falls below 220,000 within the window.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.25 percentage points in the same month signals a policy shift toward accommodative policy, which tends to boost equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by ≥0.25pp AND FEDFUNDS falls by ≥0.25pp in the same month
regime_hint: Dual normalization event (labor market easing + rate cut)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average (IC > 0.05) or the policy shift is not confirmed by subsequent inflation data.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 400,000 in a month accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a strong labor market, which can fuel consumer spending and corporate optimism, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days in expansionary regimes only.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 400,000 AND UNRATE < 4.0 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in expansion regimes (IC < 0.05), or the labor market signal is not sustained for two months.
